title: Vanishing over a local scheme spreads to an open neighborhood
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], q a nonnegative integer, and ξ a class in H^q(X,F) [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Let x be a point and g_x:Spec O_X,x → X its canonical morphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. If g_x^*(ξ)=0 under cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], there is an open neighborhood U of x [def-weil-open-immersion] such that ξ pulls back to zero along U → X.

source.place: Lemma 09AX, proof (local-ring colimit), using Tags 03Q6 and 09YQ; Cohomology on Sites Tag 03F3.

proof.text: Apply the local-ring colimit theorem to the Ext object-cohomology presheaf restricted to open neighborhoods of x, using its canonical open-to-etale inclusion. Represent the global class on the top open via the theorem's restriction comparison. Pullback composition shows that its colimit image is zero by the given vanishing over Spec O_X,x. The theorem's elementwise conclusion supplies a smaller open with zero restriction. Naturality of the comparison and injectivity of cohomology maps induced by coefficient isomorphisms remove the transports. Pullback composition then identifies this with the original global class pulled back to the smaller open.
